title: ops contingency staffing budget scratchpad
summary: Working scratchpad to map a light-weight contingency path for ops/sre/platform headcount and budget across Q1–Q4 2027. Includes a baseline budget, two stress scenarios, hire phasing swaps (defer vs. contract), and quick pricing sensitivity rules tied to token-price tiers.

sensitivity_assumptions: 1) Revenue shock: -10% top-line reduces ops hiring budget by 20% opportunity to defer non-critical FT hires. 2) Latency cost spike: +20% infrastructure spend when burst usage exceeds reserve pools; contractors recommended for short-term absorb. 3) Price elasticity of demand: token price increase of 15% -> expected demand drop 8% over 6 weeks (elasticity = -0.55). 4) GPU spot volatility: two-week average spot premium > 35% triggers switching to reserved preemptible mixes for non-critical workloads.
scenario_runs: Scenario A (conservative): apply revenue shock, defer 7 FTEs, move $1.2M to contractor pool, expected runway impact +3 months. Scenario B (balanced): hold hiring but convert 4 hires to contracts, use $0.5M reserve, implement pricing +10% on non-enterprise routes (expected demand drop 4%). Scenario C (aggressive defense): immediate 15% price lift across non-committed customers; defer all hires except critical leads; apply infrastructure throttles (pin to baseline models) -> risk: CS churn for high-usage customers.
interpretation_notes:
- Deferring hires yields immediate headcount savings but increases long-term risk on SLO attainment; map to SLAs before deferring.
- Contract swaps buy time for capacity elasticity but at higher marginal unit cost; use for burst-only functions (lab/reproductions, spike testing).
- Pricing moves more palatable if accompanied by automated routing to cheaper model variants and transparent communication to customers.
- Maintain a $300k headroom reserve to cover 6-8 weeks of unexpected spot premiums or slow billing windows.
decision_thresholds:
- If monthly revenue trend (3mo MA) drops > 8%: trigger hiring freeze and convert 50% of active offers to contractor proposals.
- If GPU spot premium > 35% sustained for 10 business days: spin up reserved instances and move non-critical workloads to preemptible pools.
- If churn of top-20 customers increases by 2% in a month following pricing test: rollback price change and apply credits; escalate to CRO.
